rules.text: Tram signal heads stand at the platform head or hang from the wire, never along the platform
Trams going straight through a junction from both directions get GO together
A two-car set starts coupled: 15.2 m between car centres on the same track, at every start stop (Sídliště Řepy fails)
With GO at a junction, cars do not wait for a tram standing (at a stop); they wait only for a moving / approaching tram
Where sources disagree (recent reconstruction), the newer one wins: the street survey of Sept 2026 over OSM
regular service always runs on the right-hand track; a double-track line has two tracks the whole way (line 37 Spojovací - Kněžská luka included)
Switches keep both control kinds: the historic overhead contacts and the new radio control; the player chooses which to use.
rules.quote: For game purposes I'm keeping both historic current switch and new radios at the same time. It costs nothing and player can choose which ones to use.

rules.text: The game shows speed signs up to 60 km/h; higher speeds are taken from the OSM (OpenRailwayMap) track data.
rules.quote: For now the game uses 60 km/h spped sign at most, higher speeds to be picked up from osm (openrailwaymap) track info.

rules.text: The T3 controls are placeholders without pedals; the pedals and the accelerator (zrychlovač) are to be researched and simulated.
rules.quote: currently there are only placeholder simplified controls without pedals, you can research that and how to simulate zrychlovač behavior.

rules.text: The game's T3 has no door- or stop-request buttons. The driver stops for any passengers waiting at a stop: the game cannot know whether they want this tram.
rules.quote: No it doesn't although the game tries to simulate request stops, another issue is passing stop where nobody waits for player's tram but you can't know if the waiting passenger want to take your tram (and their behavior is too simple, they could take any tram which gets them closer to their destination). In short driver should stop for any passengers waiting on the stop.

rules.text: Open doors block traction in the game; whether the T3 also applies a brake is open.
rules.quote: open door currently block adding power, not sure if brake is auto applied as well.

rules.text: A two-car T3 set runs with both cars' pantographs up, as in real operation.
rules.quote: for t3 we use both cars pantographs as it is in real operation

rules.text: A deck over a walkway without maxheight leaves at least 2.2-2.3 m clear and is as thick as that allows, up to 1 m (tools/zps_decks.py WALK 2.2 + MARGIN 0.1); the passages on lines 9, 17, 22, 23 and 37 have enough clearance.
rules.source: user 2026-11-10 from street view of the passages, #445 session (PR #452)
rules.quote: The underpasses have enough clearance, for walkway I would keep lower lower limit of 2.2-2.3 and then whatever slab it leaves, even though the 0.5m in your measurements could be just fine.

rules.text: Under a deck the floor is IPR's lidar, not the survey's level 0 (tools/zps_decks.py flatten); the survey's floor may be the better one only where it lies well under the lidar outside a tunnel, not yet seen enough to make a rule.
rules.source: user 2026-11-10 on the sections of the passages, #445 session (PR #452)
rules.quote: The lidar floor generally looks better and sits lower, have smooth believable curve, so I would prefer that one. Survey floor could be even lower but it's wavy and hard to asses where it's more accurate. If lidar has big difference and survey is quite a bit lower (while not being downright in tunnel then it might be the better one but I haven't seen enough examples.

trackHeights.radiusAnswersNote: The user's answers to the radius review (reports/review/track-radius.json, #197), one per place (lat, lon; an answer applies to the place where the radius would give way within 15 m of it): 'hold the radius' keeps the design radius there, 'follow the data' lets it give way within the band: down to the floor (trackGeometry vertical-radius-min, 500 m), and below it only for an answer given since the floor's date. 'outliers': 'drop' where the note says "Discard the outliers": the points the held curve misses the band at are dropped, worst first, and the curve at the design radius is fitted to the rest (the user, 2026-11-04: "Drop outliers, fit the rest": the curve follows the ground's trend). `ignore` (the user, 2026-11-07): 'switches' drops the heights between a junction's switches within `reach` m, the tracks meeting on the curve around them; 'stretch' drops the heights of `sources` along `stretch` (places every 5 m), which the curve then bridges (tools/line_heights.py answered_ignore). 'follow the ground' with an `area` (the user, 2026-11-08): the tracks in the area take the lidar ground, tighter than the floor where it needs, and the heights within BLEND_REACH around it move part way, so the edge makes no step; the later word in its area over every other radius answer; no curve there is tighter than its `radius_min` m (tools/line_heights.py answered_ground).
trackHeights.stepAnswersNote: The user's answers to the step review (reports/review/track-steps.json, #344), one per place (lat, lon; within 70 m of it). `use`: the archive's height, the curve bridging where it has none, or DI as it is. `drop`: heights over 5 cm from their smooth line go. `blend`: where heights are noisy or the curve exceeded, the mean with the survey. `radius`: 'follow' lets the radius give way within the band, 'hold' keeps it; the radius answers within reach give way to it. `toward`: each archive height moves that `share` of the way to the mean of survey and lidar (the lidar alone where they disagree over 8 cm), fading out over the reach's last 20 m. Read by tools/line_heights.py.
